answers.core: Depending on how the collision system in godot works, this could either be a simple asset called "Advanced Raycast" or something, or this would need a complete rework of the current collision system.
answers.workaround:
Colliders on rigidbodies where they are the only collider and be referenced with get_collider().get_child("name") (again, pseudocode)

Having multiple colliders on one rigidbody and having each separately referencable in runtime is basically the only real way for sandbox vehicle builder games to not get too laggy and/or hard to develop.


EDIT: another workaround was suggested by Xireael07: catalouge every instance of CollisionShape, get the shape ID with RayCast.get_collider_shape(), and find the corresponding CollisionShape that way (still, not ideal)

title: Add a method for RayCast2D that returns the actual CollisionShape2D or CollisionPolygon2D hit instead of the rigidbody
